answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, making influence depend on reachable, independently attested mass rather than self-issued links. An adversarial sybil cluster behind a sparse external cut has low conductance φ; mixing estimates and min-cut transitivity bounds limit the probability that walks enter it, mathematically capping its aggregate voting weight. The same bound applies to copper, yarrow, and ferrous labels.
